papers.title: Disruption of cellular iron homeostasis by SRPX2-IRP1 interaction aggravates renal fibrosis in chronic kidney disease.
papers.summary: SRPX2 is elevated in chronic kidney disease patients and drives renal fibrosis via TGFβ/SMAD signaling. SRPX2 physically interacts with iron regulatory protein IRP1, disrupting IRP1/iron-responsive element control: TfR1 falls while FTH1 and FPN rise, causing tubular iron dyshomeostasis. SRPX2 ablation attenuates fibrosis in mice, and iron dextran supplementation alleviates injury.

papers.title: Reducing haystacks to needles - ViralClust: A Nextflow pipeline to cluster viral sequences.
papers.summary: ViralClust is a modular Nextflow pipeline for bias-aware selection of representative viral genomes, integrating five clustering algorithms (cd-hit-est, sumaclust, vsearch, mmseqs2, hdbscan). Tested on six RNA/DNA virus datasets spanning 632 to 156,586 sequences, it reduced dataset size by ~95% or more while preserving genetic diversity, mitigating outbreak-driven sampling biases.

papers.title: Repurposing Engineered Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetases for Proximity-Dependent Protein Labeling through the Release of Aminoacyl-AMP Intermediate.
papers.summary: Engineered aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, developed to charge noncanonical amino acids, unexpectedly release the aminoacyl-AMP intermediate in the absence of cognate tRNA, covalently acylating proximal proteins. Multiple synthetases show self- and trans-labeling in vitro and in living cells; bioorthogonal amino acids enable fluorophore or biotin conjugation, establishing a multiplexable proximity-labeling approach.

papers.title: Elucidating the Requirements for microRNA-Mediated Upregulation Enables Reengineering of Upregulatory Sites.
papers.summary: Using the MirFluR dual-fluorescence reporter, the authors characterize miRNA-mediated upregulation of B3GLCT by miR-891b. Upregulation requires specific sequence elements and RNA secondary structure, is context-dependent, and shaped by local UTR structure. Sites can be reengineered to respond to alternate miRNAs, illuminating the bidirectional nature of miRNA action.

papers.title: Mechanistic study of IL-17 inhibitors in alleviating inflammation in ankylosing spondylitis by regulating Treg cell function through modulation of the Ahr signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In a proteoglycan-induced ankylosing spondylitis mouse model, the IL-17 inhibitor secukinumab reduced arthritis inflammation and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-17, IL-6, TNF-α) while activating aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling and increasing regulatory T cells with anti-inflammatory IL-10 and TGF-β. The AhR inhibitor CH-223191 reversed these benefits, defining an IL-17 inhibitor–AhR–Treg axis.

papers.title: Dynamic inter-glycan interactions regulate site-specific N-glycan maturation in human Fcγ receptor III.
papers.summary: Why the N45 glycan of human Fcγ receptor III matures poorly was probed by reciprocal glycosylation-site mutagenesis plus molecular dynamics. Adding an N64 sequon to FcγRIIIa reduced N45 maturation; removing it from FcγRIIIb had the reciprocal effect. Simulations show N45 dynamically contacts neighboring N64 and N169 glycans, reshaping its maturation environment.

papers.title: Apical actin filament turnover mediated by cyclase-associated protein coordinates non-centrosomal microtubules in epithelium.
papers.summary: In Drosophila follicular epithelium, loss of cyclase-associated protein (CAP), a conserved actin-turnover regulator, stabilizes and accumulates apical actin; the CARP domain is principal for preventing this. Excess apical actin depletes apical microtubules and mislocalizes crosslinker Shot, impairing polarized trafficking, microvillus biogenesis, and nuclear positioning—identifying CAP-dependent actin turnover as spatially regulating non-centrosomal microtubules.

papers.title: Setting up for embryogenesis: subcellular changes at the meiosis to mitosis transition.
papers.summary: This perspective reviews subcellular remodeling during the meiosis-to-mitosis transition after fertilization, when asymmetric oocyte meiotic divisions give way to the zygote's symmetric first embryonic mitosis one cell cycle later. The authors summarize recent biochemical and biophysical work on spindle, centrosome, and chromosome changes and the mechanisms regulating them.

papers.title: In vivo clustering of oskar mRNA is driven by RNA concentration, RNA binding proteins, and an RNA palindrome.
papers.summary: Combining super-resolution microscopy, single-mRNA imaging, and genetic perturbations in Drosophila embryos, this study shows oskar mRNA clustering is driven collectively by RNA concentration, Staufen, and an RNA palindrome promoting dimerization and oligomerization. Oligomerization is more perturbation-sensitive than dimerization, and palindrome-mediated base pairing may broadly govern mRNA clustering; eIF3a emerges as a candidate.

papers.title: Cdk1 and PP2A constitute a molecular switch controlling orderly degradation of atypical E2Fs.
papers.summary: E2F7 and E2F8 restrain pro-proliferative E2F1 transcription. Their amino-terminal flexible domains contain APC/C recognition motifs adjacent to threonine residues whose Cdk1 phosphorylation is rate-limiting for degradation. PP2A-mediated dephosphorylation acts as a molecular switch, coupling E2F7/8 degradation to G1 phase and the rise of E2F1, ensuring orderly APC/C substrate degradation.

papers.title: The identification of Drp1 patient mutations that limit interactions with Mff.
papers.summary: Three Drp1 patient mutations (G362S, E379K, E410K) show no apparent defects in core Drp1 functions. Using negative-stain electron microscopy, mass photometry, GTPase assays, and confocal microscopy, the authors find G362S and E410K limit interactions with the pro-fission partner Mff, inhibiting co-assembly and GTPase stimulation, while E379K forms apparently functional Mff complexes.

papers.title: Mitokines as bioenergetic stress signals in cardiovascular disease: mitochondrial communication, endocrine adaptation, and translational implications.
papers.summary: This review examines mitokines—FGF21, GDF15, and mitochondrial-derived peptides humanin and MOTS-c—as stress signals linking mitochondrial dysfunction to systemic adaptation in cardiovascular disease, emphasizing mitochondrial unfolded protein and integrated stress responses. It proposes a "mitokine code" framework, evaluates biomarker and therapeutic potential, and highlights mechanistic uncertainties for mitochondrial-derived peptides.

papers.title: Genome-wide identification of CHY zinc finger and RING finger (CHYR) genes in pepper and functional characterization of CaCHYR5 in response to Phytophthora capsici infection.
papers.summary: Genome-wide analysis identified eight CaCHYR genes in pepper, classified into three phylogenetic groups with similar conserved motifs and exon–intron structures; segmental duplication drove family expansion. Genes show tissue-specific expression and differential responses to Phytophthora capsici infection. Transient CaCHYR5 overexpression increased susceptibility, indicating a negative regulatory role in pepper defense.
